$comment: Policy for scripts/licenses.mjs. Three tiers, because the obligations differ:
production (!dev, !optional) ships in the bundle      -> must satisfy `allow`
dev                          is a build tool          -> only `denyAlways` applies
optional                     is a platform binary     -> `allow`, or a named exception
A build tool's licence does not attach to its output, which is why the dev tier
is looser. Anything not covered by a tier rule fails closed.

@img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64@1.3.2.reason: Prebuilt libvips binary, an optional dependency of sharp, itself an optional dependency of next, present only for the next/image optimizer. This app imports next/image zero times and next.config.ts sets images.unoptimized, so it is never loaded. Unmodified, dynamically linked by sharp, not statically linked into our code; LGPL-3.0 s4/s5 are satisfied by shipping the licence text and pointing at upstream source. Cannot be excluded at install time: --omit=optional would also drop @next/swc-*, @rolldown/binding-* and @unrs/resolver-binding-*, which the build genuinely needs.

@img/sharp-libvips-linuxmusl-x64@1.3.2.reason: As @img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64 above; the musl build of the same binary.

@img/sharp-wasm32@0.35.3.reason: sharp's wasm fallback, carrying the same libvips as the native binaries. npm leaves it in the tree as extraneous even after a clean `npm ci`, because it is an optional dependency for a platform we are not on; the gate treats anything undeclared as production, which is how this surfaced at all. Same standing as the two libvips entries above: never loaded (next/image is unused and images.unoptimized is set), unmodified, and the conjunction is only unallowed because of the LGPL term.
